description: A locally run sheet-music upload and analysis web app with a Flask API and HTML frontend. Containerization is a later phase and is out of scope for the initial implementation.

services.name: Flask backend
features: Expose an Import Score wizard. Its preflight checks SHA-256 first, then exact visual hash, without persistent storage for duplicates. For unique files, assign a GUID and create the resource before metadata review.

Generate a 128x128 PNG thumbnail named from the GUID upload basename, serve the latest three uploads on the home page, and provide a full /library listing with links to detail pages containing the original document and metadata.
Require the local demo user to delete a resource; the detail page confirms deletion before removing its local original/thumbnail files and redirecting home.
Require the local demo user to open the Import Score page and submit score uploads.

Add a fake hard-coded local user login/logout for the PoC, with JoinedAt profile information. Associate favorites and collection ownership with the user; public visibility and subscription behavior are deferred.
Show an uploader profile with uploaded-work count and join date on details; support favorite toggling and adding the work to an existing or new owned collection with null order/annotation.
service/UploadService stores each score under uploads/ with a GUID-based filename and passes that filename to FileProcessing.
Calculate a SHA-256 file hash before OCR or pHash; reject exact duplicates with HTTP 409, remove the newly saved file, and do not insert a resource row. Persist FileHash in accepted resource rows.

Run OCR and compare perceptual hashes using pHash and Hamming distance; the import duplicate gate compares exact visual-hash equality before OCR. Infer metadata by keyword matching OCR text against metadata field options.

Use a DataManager abstraction backed by db.json with serialized table definitions and rows modeled on server/db/create_db.sql, including the favorites table linking users and resources with the favorited date.

Insert every processed upload into the resource table with its VisualHash and local file location; compare new hashes against previously stored resource hashes so each upload is available for future matching.
Set resource OriginalName to the exact uploaded filename. Set DisplayName to the first non-empty OCR text line, falling back to the original filename without its extension.

Use a SettingsManager to load and provide configurable settings, initially the local upload storage folder and maximum pHash Hamming distance accepted as a possible match; structure it to support future settings.
Expose a reusable resource metadata update endpoint used by the import wizard and future editing pages. Return JSON for duplicate and resource creation outcomes.
Show raw OCR text, SHA-256, and visual hash in an expandable Debug panel on the import page.

After metadata review, rank reasonable matches using pHash, title, and composer; ask the user to confirm same/different without merging or changing resources. If there are no reasonable matches, state that import is complete.

services.name: HTML frontend
services.framework: Plain HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript served by Flask
features: Provide a home page with the latest three uploads and a link to the Import Score wizard.
Show the latest three uploads above the home-page upload form, each with a thumbnail and title linking to its detail page; provide a link to the full library.
Provide a full library page and detail pages with the full-size image or embedded PDF and additional metadata; show a confirmed delete action only to the logged-in demo user.
Allow any visitor to download the original document from its detail page using a title-based filename, appending composer when present and preserving the original extension; defer download counting.
Display the returned upload, OCR, duplicate-match, and inferred-metadata results.
Display ranked possible matches after metadata save, provide same/different confirmation without a merge step, and state import complete if there are no reasonable candidates.
Provide a signed-in profile page with the user's name, join date, uploads, and owned collections; support owner-scoped collection rename/delete and item removal regardless of Public visibility.

deploymentScope.initial: Run locally as a Python Flask application using local file storage; do not require Azure services or a remote database.
deploymentScope.future: Containerize the application in a later phase; do not add container configuration now.
